author: coordinator-20260921-round7
content: Round7 reusable route: use a full-interval Volterra integral equation rather than a Taylor estimate restricted to a first block whose width may vanish. Weighted normalization transfers C1 convergence to a uniform endpoint slope gap. Root isolation then controls entire blocks, not only midpoint signs. A separate thin-heavy-interval construction combines n-dimensional low-energy platforms with a codimension-n central-zero subspace to prove the fixed-n supremum limit (n+1)^2*pi^2. The local formal Wronskian declarations in lean-proof/SL/AuditRound7.lean are linked through the round7 report, with actual type/axiom scope. This does not identify finite-R optimizers or prove all-R self-consistent branches. See the exact reviewed source and round7 report.
